Findings.identity: The native STS preflight returned account 000000000000 and arn:aws:iam::000000000000:user/Delegated. EC2 calls used us-east-1 native HTTPS endpoint.
Findings.identical_request: A unique explicit ClientToken was accepted and echoed. Repeating the identical request returned the same NetworkAclId, not a second ACL.
Findings.parameter_mismatch: Changing one tag value, reversing the tag array without changing its members, or changing VpcId to a second owned VPC under the original token each returned HTTP 400 IdempotentParameterMismatch. Original tag array order is therefore significant in the observed request fingerprint.
Findings.mutation_replay: After mutating the owned ACL state tag to mutated and adding ingress TCP rule 100 for port 443, replaying the original request returned the same ACL ID and current Entries including rule 100, but its Tags contained the original request state=original. DescribeNetworkAcls both before and after replay returned state=mutated, proving replay did not overwrite stored tags. This is neither a full original-response snapshot nor an unmodified current-resource projection: current ACL entries coexist with request-time tags in CreateNetworkAcl replay output.
Findings.delete_replay: After successful DeleteNetworkAcl and a DescribeNetworkAcls InvalidNetworkAclID.NotFound, the original request returned HTTP 400 IdempotentParameterMismatch; repeating again produced the same error. A separate unmodified ACL/token also returned IdempotentParameterMismatch after deletion. VPC-filtered custom-ACL describes confirmed no recreation.
Findings.token_boundaries: Explicit empty ClientToken and a token containing non-ASCII e-acute returned HTTP 400 InvalidParameterValue. An ASCII token containing spaces and punctuation succeeded; UUID syntax is not required. A 64-character ASCII token succeeded; the corresponding 65-character token returned HTTP 400 InvalidParameterValue. A token containing U+0001 returned HTTP 400 InvalidCharacter with invalid XML character message.
Findings.expiration: Unknown. This short probe does not establish token TTL, expiration, or persistence beyond the observed deletion/replay interval. No expiration value is inferred.
Findings.scope: Only one native account and Region were exercised. Cross-account/cross-Region token scoping and omitted-token semantics were not probed here.
Findings.capture: Calls preserve exact explicit CLI input, parsed native output, response XML, HTTP status, request ID and UTC start time. No authentication/debug logs or credentials are persisted.

Cleanup.absence_confirmed: Each returned custom ACL and both owned VPCs returned the corresponding NotFound code after cleanup. VPC-filtered custom ACL inventories were empty before VPC deletion.
Cleanup.resource_safety: No default ACL was modified and no ACL was associated. VPC deletion removed only implicit children of the owned tagged VPCs. The preexisting DhcpOptionsId was observed only, never modified or deleted. No compute, subnet, public IP, gateway, endpoint or billed networking resources were created.
Cleanup.coordination: A sibling route-table probe temporarily used the same ownership tag prefix due to shared Eval globals. Its separate VPC vpc-04320d4f01d32b3c5 and route table were excluded from this fixture and never cleaned by this probe; ownership was explicitly coordinated with RouteTokenEvidence. Cleanup here was by owned resource IDs, not tag prefix.
